case_name: In re Radiology Associates, Inc. Litigation
valuation_method_relied_on: DCF (petitioner expert Danyluk's DCF as modified by court; comparable companies and capitalized-earnings approaches rejected)
court_erp_type: Ibbotson historical mean for small-cap (<$100M) stocks 1926-1986 (market premium as used by expert)
court_terminal_method: Gordon growth (discount rate minus growth)
erp_beta_preference_statement: Court rejected hypothetical industry-average capital structure (49/51) in favor of company's actual capital structure (29.63% debt/70.37% equity), and used pre-tax 9.8% cost of debt because company was nontaxable: WACC = 29.63% x 9.80% + 70.37% x 21.65% = 18.14% (rounded to 18%).
notes: Combined appraisal/fiduciary action by a radiologist squeezed out via short-form merger at $400/share. Court reduced projection growth to 5% (Delaware Trust Co. projections); terminal growth assumed 5% per Danyluk mechanics, not separately restated by court (medium confidence). Cost of equity 21.65 = 8.82 + 0.95 x 13.5. Rejected implicit minority discount adjustment. Award 2.7x merger price. Total value for 250 shares $271,000.

case_name: Gilbert v. MPM Enterprises, Inc. (Del. Ch. 1997), aff'd M.P.M. Enterprises, Inc. v. Gilbert (Del. 1999)
valuation_method_relied_on: DCF (petitioner's CAPM framework with respondent's comparable-company beta; respondent's EBITDA exit multiple 7.5x terminal); merger price and prior offers given zero weight
court_beta_source: Average Bloomberg raw beta of respondent's comparable companies (set in April 24, 1998 follow-up opinion)
court_terminal_method: Exit multiple (7.5x EBITDA, including 12% premium over comparables)
erp_beta_preference_statement: CAPM accepted for a closely held company over respondent's venture-capitalist survey cost of equity (35-45%); later opinion fixed cost of debt 9.6%, debt/total capital 5%, Bloomberg raw beta, small-company premium 2.87.
banker_dcf_criticism: Respondent expert's buy-side DCF rejected because it valued the company from the buyer's perspective.
notes: Closely held company; equity value $156,331,000 = $14,211.91/share (800 shares = $11,369,528), per Delaware Supreme Court summary of the May 22, 1998 final order. Final discount rate not stated in either opinion on CourtListener (April 1998 opinion not located). Petitioner expert Patricof (McGraw): CAPM cost of equity 20.6%, WACC 19.9%; DCF+comps 50/50. Respondent expert Advest (Lundquist): sell-side DCF $90.5M less 8.8% and 1% = $81.7M. Supreme Court affirmed zero weight to merger terms and prior offers.

case_name: M.G. Bancorporation, Inc. v. Le Beau
valuation_method_relied_on: Petitioner expert Clarke's valuation (comparable companies $76.24-$77.50, DCF $72.23-$73.96, comparable acquisitions $85) with control premium at subsidiary level; affirmed
banker_dcf_criticism: Merger price set by Sheshunoff 'fair market value' of a minority block (legally flawed basis for fair value).
notes: Short-form merger of bank holding company at $41 based on minority-block fair market value appraisal. Quote is from the Chancery opinion as quoted by the Supreme Court. Supreme Court affirmed $85 but remanded compound interest. Chancery opinion (Del. Ch. 1998) not on CourtListener.

case_name: ONTI, Inc. v. Integra Bank
valuation_method_relied_on: DCF weighted 2/3 and stock-market approach 1/3 (Eight Centers: DCF $10,034,816; market $25,800,000; weighted $15,289,877; total 40% interest $16,195,258 incl. OTI)
court_erp_type: S&P 500 risk premium (Ibbotson historical, over 90-day T-bill)
court_terminal_method: Constant Growth Valuation Model (Gordon); EBIT exit multiple rejected
erp_beta_preference_statement: Court cut Ibbotson small-stock premium from 5.2% to 2.75% to correct for 'data snooping'; allowed reduced company-specific risk premium of 1.7% (from 3.4%). Build-up discount rate: 5.5 T-bill + 8.4 S&P premium + 2.75 small stock + 1.7 company-specific = 18.35 (opinion's summary table misprints the total as 18.85%; the 18.35% figure is used in the terminal multiple and discount factors).
notes: Combined appraisal and entire fairness action (counterclaim) over cash-out mergers of privately held cancer-treatment centers; values are aggregate dollars for a 40% interest, not per share. 'petitioner' = counterclaimants' expert Ruback (13.9% discount rate, removed small-stock and company-specific premia); 'respondent' = Hempstead valuation (22.5%; original merger valuation $6,040,000 for the 40% interest). Discount rate is an all-equity build-up (equals cost of equity). key_quote_position approximate (chunk 11 of 32 at 5000 chars).

case_name: Union Illinois 1995 Investment Ltd. P'ship v. Union Financial Group, Ltd.
valuation_method_relied_on: Merger price less synergies (full weight); DCF used only as a check (court's generous-assumption DCF = $5.44)
court_beta_source: Ibbotson Cost of Capital 2001 Yearbook, SIC state commercial banks median
court_erp_type: Fama-French three-factor model (court-selected for its DCF check)
court_size_premium_applied: no (Fama-French three-factor used instead of CAPM + size premium)
erp_beta_preference_statement: Petitioner's 10.43% CAPM+size cost of capital rejected as 'unrealistically low' (implied beta only 0.3) for a troubled, highly leveraged bank; court found respondent's 16% CAPM reasonable but used the 13.53% three-factor Fama-French figure from the same Ibbotson comparison group. Declined to decide propriety of company-specific risk premiums.
notes: Private bank holding company sold at auction to First Banks. Merger price $9.40 upfront plus two possible contingent $0.80 payments; court assumed equal likelihood of none/all being paid and net of synergies = $8.74. Petitioner (O'Briens' expert Mayer) 'over $16'; respondent expert Clarke $5.06 at 18% (16% gives $5.77). Pre-DFC/Dell era example of merger-price-less-synergies reliance; fair value below merger price.

case_name: Cede & Co. v. Technicolor, Inc.
valuation_method_relied_on: DCF (Chancery valuation model of 'Perelman Plan' Technicolor affirmed, but discount rate and debt reset to law-of-the-case values)
notes: 1983 MAF/Perelman cash-out of Technicolor at $23. Chancery on remand (Dec. 31, 2003; corrected July 9, 2004) valued at $21.98 using a 19.89% discount rate; Supreme Court reversed in part, reinstating the 1991 15.28% discount rate (law of the case) -> $28.41/share. Retrial experts: Cinerama 14.6%, Technicolor 15.8%.

case_name: Montgomery Cellular Holding Co. v. Dobler
valuation_method_relied_on: Petitioner expert Sherman's framework (weighted DCF, comparable transactions, comparable companies) with Chancery adjustments; affirmed
banker_dcf_criticism: Chancery found false the controller's banker/officer testimony that the $8,102.23 merger price was based on a 10.05x EBITDA multiple (it was derived from a $470 per-POP metric).
notes: Short-form merger of cellular company by majority holder Palmer Wireless. Court fair value total $196,217,373. Respondent expert Gartrell's 'standalone' $7,840 disregarded entirely. Petitioner expert used 10-year DCF and 13.25% WACC; court's final discount rate not stated in the Supreme Court opinion. Award 2.4x merger price.

case_name: Gesoff v. IIC Industries, Inc.
valuation_method_relied_on: DCF (100% weight; respondent expert Beaton's sum-of-the-parts DCF with four court changes; midpoint of conservative $9.55 and optimistic $19.05)
court_size_premium_value: 5.33 (Ibbotson decile 10, for Agrimill, Investor, Zoko/ITE); 2.41 (decile 9, Danubius); none for Balton
erp_beta_preference_statement: Rejected specific-company risk premia (SCRP) for all subsidiaries; small-size premium applied but reduced to decile 9 for Danubius because it is in the Budapest Stock Exchange index.
banker_dcf_criticism: Jesup & Lamont (fairness opinion) found 'deeply conflicted, ostensibly hired by the special committee, but plainly loyal to CP'.
notes: Combined entire fairness class action and appraisal; controller (CP Holdings) squeeze-out tender/merger at $10.50 after Sept. 11, 2001. Holding company with foreign subsidiaries (Israel, Hungary, Africa); country risk premium applied by respondent's expert. Award 36% above deal price. Respondent expert value $9.60 (Beaton; revised report midpoint shown as $9.60 in court's table).

case_name: Delaware Open MRI Radiology Associates, P.A. v. Kessler
valuation_method_relied_on: DCF (Kessler Group expert Mitchell's build-up cost of capital adopted; sum of MRI Centers plus Delaware V opportunity at 1/3 of Delaware IV)
court_beta_source: No beta (build-up model); Ibbotson negative industry risk premium (-4.51) used as proxy for beta
erp_beta_preference_statement: Build-up model accepted where CAPM cannot be applied in pure form; industry risk premium as beta proxy; small stock premium 'consistent with a good deal of academic and practitioner thinking about CAPM'; company-specific risk premium criticized as subjective back-door cash-flow cut (Mitchell's 2% tolerated as conservative). Respondent expert Reed: Rf 4.93, ERP 7.00, size 9.16, company-specific 3.5, equity rate 24.59, WACC 21.4.
notes: Combined appraisal and entire fairness action; private physician-owned MRI-center company (400 shares). court_wacc shown is Delaware I (18.64); others: Delaware II 18.79, III 18.55, IV 15.57. Equity rate 19.52 = Rf 5.01 + ERP 7.20 - industry 4.51 + size 9.82 + company-specific 2.00. Total equity value $13,292,903.22. Fair value about 2.05x merger price. Expert per-share values not extracted.

case_name: Highfields Capital, Ltd. v. AXA Financial, Inc. (MONY Group)
valuation_method_relied_on: Combined sum-of-the-parts (actuarial) and merger-price-less-shared-synergies analyses (respondent expert's models with court alterations); DCFs evaluated but not relied on
notes: Life insurer (MONY) acquired by AXA for $31 cash. Petitioner expert Shaked: DCF $39.18 (8.9% CAPM discount rate, 5.0% IBES terminal growth, GAAP earnings) weighted 50%. Respondent expert Jachym: $20.80 overall; DCF on statutory earnings at 10% ('aggressive') = $21.83, weighted 2.5%; shared synergies $31 less $7.75. Fair value 19% below deal price - an early (pre-DFC) below-deal-price award.

case_name: Global GT LP v. Golden Telecom, Inc.
valuation_method_relied_on: DCF
court_beta_source: 2/3 Bloomberg 5-yr weekly historic raw beta (1.32) + 1/3 Ibbotson SIC 4813 composite industry beta (1.24); rejected Barra predicted beta (1.2) and Bloomberg adjusted beta (1.17)
court_erp_type: supply-side / forward-looking (petitioner expert Gompers); rejected Ibbotson historical ERP (~7.1%)
court_terminal_method: Gordon growth (perpetuity)
erp_beta_preference_statement: Landmark shift from Ibbotson historical ERP to supply-side ('to cling to the Ibbotson Historic ERP blindly gives undue weight to Ibbotson's use of a single data set'); declines Barra predicted beta as a proprietary black box ('Gompers himself could not cook me up a Barra beta') but does not reject it for future cases.
banker_dcf_criticism: Gives no weight to the $105 merger price (controller-influenced process); notes Credit Suisse fairness DCF would have had a median of $110 with updated inputs.
notes: Court plugged its inputs into petitioner's (Gompers) DCF model. Rf not extracted. Growth 5.0% reflects Russian nominal (inflation) environment. Affirmed, 11 A.3d 214 (Del. 2010).

case_name: Golden Telecom, Inc. v. Global GT LP
valuation_method_relied_on: DCF (affirmed)
notes: Affirmance; also affirms acceptance of litigation tax rate differing from proxy. Numeric inputs carried from Chancery opinion (not restated).

case_name: In re Appraisal of Ancestry.com, Inc.
valuation_method_relied_on: deal price (DCF $31.79 used as check)
court_beta_source: weekly regression vs. S&P 500 (rejected respondent expert's monthly observation period, 1.30)
court_terminal_method: Gordon growth (value-driver form with 4.8% plowback)
erp_beta_preference_statement: Both experts agreed supply-side Ibbotson ERP appropriate; court used 2013 edition. Prefers weekly over monthly beta observation.
banker_dcf_criticism: Management projections ('October Scenarios') found problematic (prepared with board urging to 'modestly increase the growth rates'), a reason for preferring deal price.
notes: Unusual: petitioner's expert (Wisialowski) used lower terminal growth (3.0%) than respondent's (Jarrell 4.5%), with offsetting plowback assumptions. Equity weight 95%, Kd 3.81%, tax 38%. DCF scenarios A $30.33 / B $33.24.

case_name: Merlin Partners LP v. AutoInfo, Inc.
valuation_method_relied_on: Merger price (full weight; respondent's cost-savings deduction rejected); court DCF ($0.93 at 17.57% WACC on Base Case Projections) used as a check
erp_beta_preference_statement: Court refused to reduce the size premium below that implied by actual size (following Gearreald v. Just Care): illiquidity in the size premium relates to the company's cost of capital and is part of going-concern value.
banker_dcf_criticism: Noted that Stephens (company's banker) used a size premium and WACC even higher than respondent's expert.
notes: Micro-cap public company sold via auction to Comvest. Petitioner expert Puglisi: $2.60 (equal weight DCF and two multiples). Respondent expert Zmijewski: $0.967 (merger price less cost savings). Respondent bore burden on cost-savings adjustment and failed. Pre-DFC example of deal-price reliance.

case_name: Owen v. Cannon (Energy Services Group)
valuation_method_relied_on: DCF (2013 management projections; court blended experts' inputs; tax-affected S-corp earnings at 22.71%)
court_terminal_method: Gordon growth (mid-year convention)
erp_beta_preference_statement: Terminal growth: 'considerable precedent in Delaware for adopting a terminal growth rate that is a premium, such as 100 basis points, over inflation' (as quoted in Dunmire, citing Owen at *26).
banker_dcf_criticism: Petitioner argued the company's financial advisor (Grant Thornton fairness valuation) applied incorrect assumptions, chiefly the tax rate.
notes: Combined appraisal and entire fairness action; closely held S-corp (ESG) squeeze-out of 1,320,000 shares at $19.95 ($26.334M). Court fair value of the stake $42,165,920, i.e., $31.94/share (computed: 42,165,920 / 1,320,000). Petitioner originally derived 13.28% WACC but accepted respondent's 14.13%. Respondent expert Jacobs: DCF of cash flows $53.1M plus $11.9M net cash (per-share figure not extracted). Court's enterprise value $124,567.0K incl. cash.

case_name: LongPath Capital, LLC v. Ramtron International Corp.
valuation_method_relied_on: Merger price less synergies ($3.10 - $0.03); DCF rejected because management projections unreliable
notes: Hostile cash acquisition (by Cypress Semiconductor) at a 71% premium to $1.81 unaffected. Respondent claimed $0.34 synergies; court adopted petitioner's $0.03 estimate. Petitioner's $4.96 combined DCF and comparable transactions (two observations). Projections deemed unreliable (prepared outside ordinary course, under threat of hostile bid) - the Ramtron reliability factors later quoted in HFF.

case_name: Merion Capital LP v. BMC Software, Inc.
valuation_method_relied_on: deal price (court DCF $48.00 as check)
court_erp_type: supply-side (petitioner expert); rejected respondent's historical ERP
court_terminal_method: Gordon growth; midpoint of inflation and GDP
erp_beta_preference_statement: 'this Court has recently tended to employ the supply side ERP approach' but notes vigorous debate and that 'scholarship may dictate other approaches in the future.'
banker_dcf_criticism: Management projections 'harbored something of a bias towards optimism'; experts' DCFs 'dismayingly divergent'.
notes: Petitioner expert growth = midpoint of inflation/GDP + 50bp (rejected); respondent expert used inflation only. Footnote: midpoint of experts' discount rates (10.8%) would give $46.44. Petitioner expert Steffen; respondent expert Ruback.

case_name: In re Appraisal of Dell Inc.
valuation_method_relied_on: DCF
court_beta_source: company-specific regression, weekly observations over two years (respondent expert Hubbard); rejected peer-derived 1.35
court_terminal_method: Gordon growth (perpetuity)
erp_beta_preference_statement: Adopts supply-side ERP (6.11%) citing Golden Telecom; prefers company-specific beta over peer beta where company had few peers.
notes: Equal-weighted two DCFs (adjusted BCG 25% case $16.43; adjusted Bank Case $18.81). Court said 3% growth 'could be more appropriate' but used 2%. Equity weight 75%; cost of debt 4.95%. Reversed by Del. Supreme Court (Dell v. Magnetar, 2017). Note: deal consideration $13.75 'Final Merger Consideration'; petitioner=Cornell, respondent=Hubbard.

case_name: In re Appraisal of DFC Global Corp.
valuation_method_relied_on: blend (1/3 DCF $13.07, 1/3 comparable multiples $8.07, 1/3 deal price $9.50)
court_beta_source: 5-year smoothed (Blume-adjusted) Bloomberg weekly betas of 6 peers + DFC, Hamada unlevered/relevered at 74% debt/capital; rejected Barra-only and raw 2-year betas
court_erp_type: supply-side (Duff & Phelps); agreed by both experts
court_terminal_method: two-stage Gordon growth
erp_beta_preference_statement: Accepts smoothed (2/3 raw + 1/3 market) beta as capturing mean reversion; adopts Duff & Phelps supply-side ERP; rejects Duff & Phelps Risk Premium Report size premium for SIC-6 financial firm.
notes: Appendix A/B give all inputs. Respondent expert Beaulne DCF $7.81, multiples $8.07; petitioner expert Dages DCF $17.90. Fair value later revised to $10.30 on reargument (not separately verified here); reversed/remanded by Del. Supreme Court (DFC v. Muirfield, 2017).

case_name: Dunmire v. Farmers & Merchants Bancorp of Western Pennsylvania, Inc.
valuation_method_relied_on: Discounted net income model (single-stage capitalization, mid-year Gordon growth) - deal price rejected (controller on both sides, no sale process)
court_beta_source: Duff & Phelps 2014 Industry Cost of Capital, SIC 602 median raw OLS unlevered beta (company virtually debt-free)
court_erp_type: Long-horizon supply-side (D&P 2014 Valuation Handbook), chosen over 6.96 historical and Duke CFO survey 3.55
court_terminal_method: Gordon growth (capitalized net income, mid-year convention)
erp_beta_preference_statement: Supply-side ERP 6.18% adopted over historical 6.96% following Golden Telecom; Duke CFO survey ERP (3.55%) rejected as not widely used and outcome-driven; beta type must match size-premium type (OLS beta with OLS size premium); unlevered beta used for a debt-free bank; levered betas and small-composite betas (0.43) rejected. Court expressed no opinion on size-premium debate but applied it as integral to both experts' methods.
notes: Stock-for-stock merger of community bank into affiliate controlled by Snyder family (exchange ratio 2.17 implied $83/share). Court's discount rate is a cost of equity applied to net income (equity model for a bank), not a WACC: 2.87 + 0.7 x 6.18 + 3.87 = 11.07. Equity value $70,564,156 / 767,799 shares. Opinion cites 3% growth as 100bp over inflation precedent (Owen v. Cannon).

case_name: Merion Capital L.P. v. Lender Processing Services, Inc.
valuation_method_relied_on: deal price (court DCF $38.67 within 4%, given no weight)
court_beta_source: respondent expert's average of 5-yr monthly and 2-yr weekly betas; court said 2-yr weekly (1.503) defensible but used lower figure because it favored petitioners; rejected 5-yr daily 0.845
court_terminal_method: Gordon growth (between inflation and nominal GDP)
erp_beta_preference_statement: Prefers 2-year beta when 5-year window spans structural change (Great Recession); both experts used supply-side ERP. Declines size premium (adding 0.92% would raise WACC to 10.2%).
notes: Equity weight 70%, Kd 5.02%, tax 37%. Final merger consideration $37.14 (opinion also once states $37.04 - typo in source). Beta drove bulk of expert gap (Hausman's beta in Fischel's model = $51.18).

case_name: In re Appraisal of PetSmart, Inc.
valuation_method_relied_on: deal price (DCF rejected: management projections unreliable)
erp_beta_preference_statement: Records expert testimony that Barra betas 'have yet to be accepted by the Delaware Chancery Court'; court did not resolve beta.
banker_dcf_criticism: Petitioners alleged JPMorgan 'stretched' to a double-digit WACC (using Barra predicted/historical betas and low-quartile peer betas) to deflate DCF and support fairness opinion; banker testified it could not have rendered its fairness opinion with a lower WACC. Court found no credible evidence of manipulation.
notes: Respondent relied on deal price; respondent expert Metrick's DCF inputs (WACC 6.35%, g 2.0%) cited; DCF on management projections ranged $128.78-$133.84 per petitioners. 'Garbage in, garbage out.' Morgan Stanley early DCF range $77/$88/$100.

case_name: In re Appraisal of SWS Group, Inc.
valuation_method_relied_on: DCF (deal price given no weight; synergy-driven deal)
court_beta_source: petitioner expert's blended median of company and peer betas; rejected respondent's 2-yr weekly company beta (1.18) as affected by 'merger froth'
court_terminal_method: Gordon growth; midpoint of inflation (2.3%) and long-term economic growth (4.4%)
erp_beta_preference_statement: Supply-side ERP described as 'essentially the default method' in Chancery appraisal. Size premium split the difference (2.69% vs 4.22%) at 3.46%.
notes: Respondent's own expert valued below deal price ($5.17) arguing shared synergies; court awarded below-deal value. Deal consideration (50% stock) fell to $6.92 by closing. Affirmed by Del. Supreme Court (Halcyon v. SWS, 2018) - not separately extracted.

case_name: ACP Master, Ltd. v. Sprint Corp. / ACP Master, Ltd. v. Clearwire Corp.
valuation_method_relied_on: DCF (respondent expert's APV-based DCF adopted in full)
court_terminal_method: Gordon growth; midpoint of inflation and GDP growth
erp_beta_preference_statement: 'Without a valid explanation, the use of a generic growth rate is inherently flawed and unreasonable' (quoting Dobler) - rejects GDP growth tied to rejected projections.
banker_dcf_criticism: Notes Centerview fairness opinion used perpetuity growth rates of 1-3%.
notes: 12.44% is Cornell's all-equity (unlevered) APV discount rate; 10.92% is its WACC-equivalent per petitioner expert Jarrell (court_wacc field holds the WACC-equivalent; court_cost_of_equity holds the all-equity rate). Final merger consideration $5.00 (initial $2.97). Award was 57% below deal price; consolidated with entire-fairness claim. Affirmed (Del. 2018). Deal price $5.00 taken from case background (verified).

case_name: DFC Global Corp. v. Muirfield Value Partners, L.P.
valuation_method_relied_on: reversed Chancery blend ($10.30 after reargument, DCF $13.33 at 4.0% growth); remanded with instruction that deal price deserved heavy weight
notes: Supreme Court; reviews perpetuity growth vs. risk-free-rate ceiling debate (Chancery had capped g at Rf 3.14%, then raised to 4.0% on reargument). Petitioner expert used 3-stage model with 2.7% terminal growth and alternate 2-stage at 3.1%.

case_name: Dell, Inc. v. Magnetar Global Event Driven Master Fund Ltd.
valuation_method_relied_on: reversed exclusive-DCF award; directs heavy weight to deal price/market data (remanded)
banker_dcf_criticism: Criticizes litigation-expert DCFs: 'each party ... enlisted highly paid, well-credentialed experts to produce DCF valuations ... But their valuations landed galaxies apart'; calls the Chancery DCF value 'the antithesis of any economist's definition of fair market value'.
notes: Supreme Court reversal of Chancery's $17.62 DCF award. Text OCR has typos ('mbre', 'markét') corrected in quote. Not a fair-value-setting decision.

case_name: Verition Partners Master Fund Ltd. v. Aruba Networks, Inc.
valuation_method_relied_on: unaffected market price (30-day average); DCFs rejected
erp_beta_preference_statement: Notes court precedent treats inflation as the floor for terminal growth; some precedent (DFC) treats risk-free rate as ceiling; 'expresses no view'. Criticizes petitioner expert's low beta (0.91) as ~35% below Aruba's 5-yr adjusted weekly beta.
banker_dcf_criticism: Uses bankers' fairness valuations (mean midpoint $26.57) and analyst targets ($23.4) as market indicators against which petitioner's DCF diverged.
notes: Rf 2.75% was common to both experts (not a court finding per se). Respondent expert Dages chose growth = risk-free rate citing DFC trial opinion. Reversed by Del. Supreme Court (2019), which awarded deal price less synergies $19.10.

case_name: In re Appraisal of AOL Inc.
valuation_method_relied_on: DCF (full weight; deal price used as check only)
court_terminal_method: two-stage Gordon growth (rejected 3-stage and 10-yr projections)
banker_dcf_criticism: Notes respondent expert benchmarked growth to analyst/advisor perpetuity growth rates (range 1.0%-6.6%, median 2.5%).
notes: Court built on respondent expert Fischel's DCF ($44.85) +$1.28 (growth to 3.5%) +$2.57 (Display Deal). Discount rate apparently undisputed / not stated in opinion. Deal process not 'Dell Compliant' due to CEO's 'done deal' statements. Later Aug. 2018 opinion (cluster 4526785) addressed reargument (not separately extracted). Below-deal-price DCF award.

case_name: Blueblade Capital Opportunities LLC v. Norcraft Companies, Inc.
valuation_method_relied_on: DCF (court's own; deal price rejected due to flawed process)
court_beta_source: median unlevered 2-yr weekly beta of 6 guideline public companies (0.98, Hamada, gross debt) relevered at 75/25 equity/debt
court_terminal_method: Gordon growth (perpetuity growth method, as both experts)
banker_dcf_criticism: Cites Matthews & Rosenbloom critique of the 'unwarranted assumption that capex should equal depreciation' in terminal year; adjusts terminal FCF accordingly. Citi's DCF/comps range $16.75-$27 noted.
notes: Respondent proffered deal price less synergies ($21.90). Pre-tax cost of debt 6.40% (post-tax 3.97%, 38% tax). ERP 6.21% and Rf 2.75% common to experts (type not labeled in snippet). Text is OCR ('Hainada' = Hamada).

case_name: In re Appraisal of Solera Holdings, Inc.
valuation_method_relied_on: deal price less synergies
court_terminal_method: n/a (both experts used 3-stage DCFs; court gave no weight)
erp_beta_preference_statement: Terminal-period dispute: ROIC-converges-to-WACC model (respondent, 'a theory this court has repeatedly cited with approval') vs. perpetual 'moat' excess returns; plowback 37.1% (Damodaran/Koller) vs 16.4% (Bradley-Jarrell inflation formula), a $23.90/share swing.
banker_dcf_criticism: Notes ~88% of petitioners' enterprise value came from periods after the 5-year projections; DCF 'subject to manipulation and guesswork'.
notes: Respondent's unaffected-price argument ($36.39, post-Aruba) rejected as 'facially incredible'. 'unaffected_price' here is respondent's asserted figure. Petitioner expert Cornell; respondent expert Hubbard.

case_name: Verition Partners Master Fund Ltd. v. Aruba Networks, Inc.
valuation_method_relied_on: deal price less synergies (respondent's own estimate)
notes: Supreme Court itself fixed fair value at deal price less synergies; criticized reliance on unaffected market price as double-counting agency costs. Chancery's own deal-less-synergies estimate had been $18.20.

case_name: In re Appraisal of Jarden Corp.
valuation_method_relied_on: unaffected market price (court DCF $48.13 as corroboration; deal-less-synergies ~$46.21 questioned)
court_beta_source: respondent expert Hubbard's Jarden-specific beta; peer/comparable betas disregarded; close to petitioner's 5-yr weekly company beta 1.24
court_erp_type: supply-side (Duff & Phelps); rejected respondent's midpoint of historical 6.9% and supply-side
court_terminal_method: value-driver formula NOPLAT(1-g/RONIC)/(WACC-g), RONIC 11.2%
erp_beta_preference_statement: 'strong support for the use of the forward-looking Supply-Side ERP in the valuation literature'; midpoint ERP 'lacks any methodological foundation'. Size premium endorsed as empirical correction to CAPM ('the CAPM should include a size premium when appropriate').
banker_dcf_criticism: Footnote: court's 6.94% WACC 'is within the range calculated by Centerview but below the WACC calculated by Goldman Sachs, Deutsche Bank, RBC and Barclays.'
notes: Terminal investment rate dispute = 87% of expert DCF gap; court set TIR at midpoint of 33.9% and 21.6%. Kd 2.8% after-tax(?) / 35% tax, 63.9% equity. Affirmed, Fir Tree v. Jarden (Del. 2020). Petitioner's $71.35 was comparable-companies; his DCF was $70.36-$70.40. Respondent's expert ERP was hybrid; respondent expert Hubbard testified he 'prefer[s] the historical risk premium'.

case_name: In re Appraisal of Columbia Pipeline Group, Inc.
valuation_method_relied_on: deal price (no synergy deduction); DCF not used
erp_beta_preference_statement: Contrasts petitioner expert's 5-yr weekly beta with bankers' 2-yr weekly (Columbia advisors) and 1-yr daily (TransCanada advisor) betas; 2-yr weekly would cut DCF to $18.10.
banker_dcf_criticism: Petitioner's 3.0% perpetuity growth vs. Lazard's implied 1.4%-1.9% and Goldman's 1%-2% (Proxy); cutting to 1.5% gives $17.28. Collects cases criticizing exit-multiple terminal values as 'little more than a special case of the comparable companies approach' (Gray v. Cytokine; Gholl; Prescott). Goldman fairness DCF $18.64-$23.50; Lazard $18.88-$25.50.
notes: Respondent's expert Zmijewski valued synergies (DCF NPV $4.64/sh) but court found none were shared; awarded deal price. Petitioner expert Jeffers. Respondent did not present a standalone DCF.

case_name: In re Appraisal of Stillwater Mining Co.
valuation_method_relied_on: deal price; DCF not used
erp_beta_preference_statement: Size premium: 'The scholarly literature on whether and how to apply a size premium is less than enlightening' (Fama-French, Asness 'Size Matters If You Control Your Junk', Damodaran 'Where is the Beef?', Ang); size-premium dispute = $2.13/sh (24% of gap). ERP: respondent's Duff & Phelps historical supply-side 5.97% (without 1.08% WWII interest-rate-bias deduction) vs petitioner's Damodaran implied forward-looking 5.34% ($1.33/sh swing).
notes: Respondent expert Zmijewski applied 1.66% D&P size premium; petitioner expert Rosen applied none (alt. 1.5% Ibbotson). Affirmed, Brigade v. Stillwater (Del. 2020).

case_name: Manichaean Capital, LLC v. SourceHOV Holdings, Inc.
valuation_method_relied_on: DCF (petitioner expert Meinhart's DCF/capital cash flow model adopted in toto except size premium)
court_beta_source: Guideline-company betas, Hamada relevered (1.37/2.46/2.02 across capital structures); unlevered 1.21 (highest guideline unlevered beta) for CCF
erp_beta_preference_statement: Court chose decile-9 D&P size premium 2.68% over 2.08%, noting circularity since market cap is an indicator of fair value.
notes: Private company (Business Combination with Quinpario/Exela); no deal-price appraisal; Business Combination implied $4,177.10/share. Respondent APV (Jarrell) $2,817 (originally $1,723). Exhibit WACC table (11.6% selected; CCF pretax 12.9%) reflects Meinhart's model with 2.68% size premium as shown in court's appendix; court WACC therefore medium confidence. Valuation weighted 50/50 lender-model DCF and CCF.

case_name: In re Appraisal of Panera Bread Co.
valuation_method_relied_on: deal price less synergies ($11.56 cost/tax synergies)
court_terminal_method: n/a (DCFs disregarded; dispute over investment rate IR=g/RONIC with RONIC=WACC)
erp_beta_preference_statement: Respondent expert set RONIC equal to WACC in terminal period ('[i]n a competitive industry, abnormal profits tend to vanish over time').
banker_dcf_criticism: Morgan Stanley internal notes: 'You've got to believe that 80+% of your value is in the terminus ... there is always risk of execution which may not be captured by our calculated WACC.' MS DCF ranges: street case $231-$318, management case $300-$410.
notes: Petitioners' $361 = 60% DCF ($354) / 30% comps / 10% precedents. Respondent expert Hubbard DCF $291.71 (corroborative only); respondent post-trial argued $293.44. Respondent prepaid $315 and was denied a refund of the $11.56 difference.

case_name: Fir Tree Value Master Fund, LP v. Jarden Corp.
valuation_method_relied_on: unaffected market price (affirmed)
court_terminal_method: McKinsey value-driver formula (affirmed); TIR on reargument 27.75% (avg of 33.9% and 21.6%)
notes: Supreme Court rejects argument that deal price is a floor for fair value. Chancery reargument opinion (Sept. 2019, cluster 4661913) corrected TIR application.

case_name: Kruse v. Synapse Wireless, Inc.
valuation_method_relied_on: DCF (court-modified; adopted respondent expert Noe's margins, 12% WACC and Gordon growth terminal value)
court_beta_source: Industry estimates (Duff & Phelps 2015 Valuation Handbook - Industry Cost of Capital), average of 32 companies
court_terminal_method: Gordon growth
erp_beta_preference_statement: Rejected respondent's 40% venture-capital 'probability of failure' discount rate (company-specific risk) and petitioner's all-equity CAPM (Rf 2.68 20-yr, ERP 6.03, full-information beta 1.01, size premium 5.4 = 14.2%).
notes: Private company squeeze-out at settlement-set price; no market evidence, neither side argued deal price. Fair value $0.228 is BELOW the $0.42899 merger price. Respondent expert Noe gave range $0.06-$0.11 (no single value). Petitioner expert Sweet used exit multiple 21.9x (court rejected). Court WACC is industry-based 12% (no CAPM build reported).

case_name: In re Appraisal of Regal Entertainment Group
valuation_method_relied_on: Deal price less synergies ($23.00 - $3.77 = $19.23) plus $4.37 Tax Act adjustment between signing and closing; petitioner DCF evaluated but not relied on
banker_dcf_criticism: Noted Cineworld's advisors' DCF midpoint was $25.70 on analyst consensus vs $36.40 on the 2017 Projections; Morgan Stanley DCF range $20.99-$28.12; 2017 Projections deemed optimistic.
notes: Respondent's $18.02 = equal weighting of unaffected trading price and deal-price-less-synergies. Unaffected $15.74 is the closing price on Nov 1, 2017 (46.1% premium) per opinion. Petitioner DCF at pre-Tax-Act rate = $26.51. Fair value slightly ABOVE deal price because of post-signing Tax Act value increase. Court DCF inputs not determined.

case_name: BCIM Strategic Value Master Fund, LP v. HFF, Inc.
valuation_method_relied_on: Adjusted deal price (deal price at signing less net synergies = $44.29) plus $2.30 increase in value between signing and closing; petitioner DCF ($56.19) evaluated but not relied on
erp_beta_preference_statement: Petitioner expert's supply-side ERP 6.14% described as endorsed by the court (citing Golden Telecom, Orchard); 20-year Treasury as of day before closing is 'standard practice'; court defended selecting beta with attention to standard errors (Damodaran, Pratt & Grabowski, Duff & Phelps) against Hubbard's critique; size premium undisputed.
banker_dcf_criticism: Morgan Stanley DCF relied on 2019 budget and did not incorporate value from deal pipeline.
notes: Deal consideration was cash $24.63 + 0.1505 JLL shares: $49.46 at price agreement (Feb 17, 2019), $49.16 at signing announcement, $45.87 at closing. deal_price field uses $49.16 (signing). Fair value $46.59 is below signing value but above closing-date consideration. Respondent $44.29 = upper bound of fair value. Petitioner: DCF $56.19, adjusted trading price $58.68, 90/10 weighting = $56.44. Hubbard's synergy DCF used 11.16% discount rate. Company had only a one-year budget, so the expert built litigation projections.

case_name: HBK Master Fund L.P. v. Pivotal Software, Inc.
valuation_method_relied_on: 50/50 blend of adjusted comparable companies ($14.75) and court-adjusted respondent DCF ($16.13 in corrected opinion; $14.91 in original Aug 2023 opinion op 9555735); deal price not given deference despite MFW
court_beta_source: CAPM per respondent expert Lehn (not detailed)
court_terminal_method: Gordon growth (court rejected respondent's 'convergence' approach implying 0% growth)
erp_beta_preference_statement: Size premium rejected; proponent bears burden; cites Damodaran 'Where is the beef?' critique calling continued use 'inertia'.
banker_dcf_criticism: Court's 2.5% growth noted as within the range the respondent's financial adviser (Morgan Stanley) used in its fairness opinion.
notes: Controller (VMware) squeeze-out with MFW conditions; court held appraisal statute does not require deference to deal price in MFW controller deals. Petitioners relied on comps/precedent transactions (no DCF). Respondent DCFs: $13.83 (7.69% WACC) and $11.87 (8.97% WACC), averaged ~$12.17 with convergence terminal (effective 0% growth). Corrected opinion (Mar. 12, 2024; op 9950150) raised the DCF output to $16.13 and fair value to $15.44, i.e., ABOVE the $15 deal price; original Aug. 14, 2023 opinion (op 9555735) had $14.91 DCF / $14.83 fair value. Inputs (7.69% WACC, 2.5% g) unchanged.

case_name: Hyde Park Venture Partners Fund III, L.P. v. FairXchange, LLC
valuation_method_relied_on: Deal price ($330 million at signing = $10.42/share) as 'least bad' method, though neither party asked for it; petitioner DCF rejected (Series C projections too speculative); no synergy deduction or signing-to-closing adjustment
notes: Private early-stage futures exchange acquired by Coinbase ($265M stock + $65M cash). Consideration fell to $310.4M by closing; court used $330M signing value. Respondent (selling stockholders) argued ceilings ($154M in pre-trial brief); expert said value below $310.4M. Petitioner per-share DCF value not extracted. Rule 409A valuation found stale/unreliable.

case_name: Jacobs v. Akademos, Inc.
valuation_method_relied_on: Respondent expert's DCF/standalone value ($2.4M-$4.3M) below preferred stock liquidation preference; common stock worth zero (contingent claims analysis also yields $0)
notes: Combined appraisal and entire fairness action over venture-backed ed-tech company merger with controller (KV Fund). Petitioner DCF rejected because it relied on optimistic Confidential Information Presentation projections incl. unfunded new business lines. Fair value of common = $0.

case_name: Gladstone v. EBC Holdings, Inc. (Firebrand Financial Group)
valuation_method_relied_on: Single-stage capitalization of normalized free cash flow (petitioner expert Margolin's framework with court-modified inputs) plus cash, securities portfolio, less subordinated loan, cross-ownership allocation
court_beta_source: Median cash-adjusted unlevered guideline-company beta (petitioner expert)
court_terminal_method: Gordon growth (capitalization of normalized cash flow)
erp_beta_preference_statement: Both experts used Kroll supply-side ERP 6.22% (court adopted); petitioner expert noted Damodaran implied-ERP alternative but kept supply-side because no consensus; size premium 4.8% market-cap based (Kroll) preferred over 5.35% revenue-based proxy as 'more consistent with Delaware appraisal practice'; growth must be consistent with reinvestment (Damodaran).
notes: Stock-for-stock reorganization of holding company above SPAC-underwriting broker-dealer (EarlyBirdCapital); no cash deal price. Court cost of equity = 3.31 + 1.35 x 6.22 + 4.80 = 16.51 (all-equity; equals discount rate). Respondent Atkins: equity DDM, 14.3% cost of equity, levered beta 1.00, 2.0% growth; values $7.00-$7.29 with GPC; final position DDM $6.79. Petitioner Margolin range topped at $18.50 (assumes 81.5% allocation and $47.8M securities).
